newsitem.title: JORDAN: Chirac appeals for Iraq oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: Chirac appeals for Iraq oil-for-food deal.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, warning of a humanitarian disaster, appealed to the international community on Thursday to make good on an agreement to allow Iraq to sell limited amounts of oil to buy food.

Chirac said in a speech to the Jordanian parliament: "France is alarmed at the humanitarian situation in Iraq and calls solemnly on the international community to apply at long last Resolution 986, which provides for the resumption of oil exports against the purchase of food and medicine to save innocent lives from tragedy."

In an indirect reference to the United States, which is holding up implementation of the resolution, agreed last May, Chirac said: "The Iraqi people cannot be held responsible for decisions to which it was not party, nor can it be held hostage for stakes that are alien to it.
"The way ahead is clear, and involves the implementation of all Security Council resolutions." He won thunderous applause.

In September, Washington blocked implementation of the first easing of the U.N. embargo imposed on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in 1990 after a renewed confrontation with Baghdad over Iraq's intervention in fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq.
In New York, U.N. diplomats said it could take months to put the oil-for-food plan into practice because the United States is blocking an oil pricing formula.
